context: Current closing price of United Airlines (UAL): $133.32 USD as of 2026-07-02.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift from what I'd assume was a recent price around 133–134, based on the typical behavior of a liquid financial asset with slight positive momentum or carry. At the one-day horizon, I anchored close to the last observed price since overnight moves in most instruments are relatively contained absent a specific catalyst, giving a point estimate of 133.8. For the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to 134.5, reflecting a small positive drift assumption while acknowledging that a week is long enough for meaningful price discovery. At one month, the estimate of 136.0 incorporates a modest continuation of that drift, though the signal becomes weaker and mean-reversion forces or macro shifts can dominate over that timeframe.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to reflect realized volatility scaling across time horizons. Daily volatility in many liquid instruments — equities, ETFs, or currency pairs in this price range — tends to run in the neighborhood of 0.5–1.5%, which justified a fairly tight 90% CI of roughly ±5 points around the one-day estimate. Over a week, volatility scales by roughly the square root of time, so the interval widens to about ±10–11 points. Over a month, it widens further to roughly ±24 points, reflecting the compounding uncertainty of approximately 20 trading days. These widths also embed uncertainty about the underlying regime — whether the asset is trending, mean-reverting, or subject to structural breaks.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these stated intervals include sudden macroeconomic data surprises such as an unexpected inflation print, central bank policy shifts, or geopolitical shocks that cause gap moves well beyond normal volatility bounds. At the daily horizon, a major earnings release, a policy announcement, or a liquidity event could easily push the price outside the 128.5–139.1 range. At the monthly horizon, a broader risk-off or risk-on regime shift — think a banking stress event, a major geopolitical escalation, or an unexpected pivot by a major central bank — could push the asset well beyond the 112–160 range. Fat tails in financial returns mean that the stated 90% CI, by construction, excludes the 10% of outcomes that could be extreme.

It is also worth acknowledging model uncertainty itself as a source of risk. Without knowing the exact instrument, I cannot tailor volatility estimates precisely, so my intervals carry additional epistemic uncertainty on top of the aleatory uncertainty from market randomness. If this asset has options markets, implied volatility derived from those would give a sharper, market-consensus view of uncertainty that might be narrower or wider than my assumed ranges depending on current conditions.
